correctness.rationale: Both line-chart restrictions of C_{q,k} factor into the simple (q+1)-point Frobenius binary form and a nonzero residual quadratic with discriminant 4 times the same dual quartic D_k. Its singular equations are equivalent to a repeated root of G_k in all odd characteristics, explicitly separating p=3 and p=7; a repeated root with k in F_q would be F_q-rational, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence D_k is smooth geometrically integral genus 3. Counting rational tangent incidences proves N1=#D_k(F_q), N0=N2=(q²+q+1-N1)/2, and the Hasse–Weil error. The source separately supplies rational smoothness. The included verifier symbolically checks discriminants and repeated-root identities and tests all admissible parameters in thirteen prime and three quadratic finite fields; finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The complete original eight-page arXiv preprint was inspected: its Theorem 1.2 identifies the rational-point smoothness criterion G_k; Proposition 1.3 supplies a good parameter; Proposition 3.3 excludes rational line components; Conjecture 1.5 asks global geometric smoothness. It does not state the smooth dual quartic D_k, tangent-line count N1=#D_k(F_q), equality N0=N2, rational flex or bitangent counts, or Weil error. Related degree-(q+2) plane-filling work and a separate degree-(q-1) rational two-contact count are not logically covering. Public research-record searches of exact formula, aliases, and larger principles found no covering theorem; general projective duality/foliation results and unindexed work remain priority risks.
residual_risks: Unindexed papers or a general foliation/branch-divisor theorem may contain the same tangent-discriminant formula or a stronger one.
Homma was checked from abstract/bibliographic scope, not complete primary full text, so general implications were not categorically excluded.
Public mathematical research-record results are not exhaustive and absence of hits is not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The new dual genus-three discriminant controls natural tangency/flex/bitangent incidence invariants of the published high-degree plane-filling family for every odd finite field and every eligible parameter. It gives exact counts by a fixed-degree auxiliary curve and a uniform O(sqrt(q)) asymptotic for nearly half the rational lines, a substantive infinite-family structural relation rather than a finite census or routine restatement. It does not rely on proving the separate open global smoothness conjecture.
